instructions.read_this_first: This single file contains everything needed to translate this batch: instructions, glossary, and the Chinese source data. No other file is needed. Output your translation as a NEW top-level key 'translated' in a copy of this same JSON structure (or as a separate file if you prefer -- either way, mirror the 'source_data.tables' shape exactly, table by table).
instructions.game_context: Personal fan-translation patch for a Chinese mobile RPG, One Piece Burning Will (Longwang private server). This batch is entirely BUFF / STATUS-EFFECT text: burn, poison, bleed, shock, and similar combat status names and their tooltip descriptions, drawn from 8 different tables that all serve the same role (a buff/debuff registry) across different game subsystems (general combat, naval fortress mode, camp buffs, sea exploration, boss fights, island trials).
instructions.scope: Translate every row's Chinese text field(s) to English. This is pure status-effect/combat-tooltip text, not story or dialogue -- there is no ambiguity about whether it is in scope, translate all of it.
instructions.critical_bundle_divergence_rule: Read source_data.header first, specifically 'content_diverges_between_bundles' per table. Some tables here have MAJOR divergence -- e.g. TableBuffGroupRule has 150 ids where the two bundle copies name completely different buffs/skills, not just reworded text, plus hundreds of ids that only exist in one bundle or the other. Where a table has content_diverges_between_bundles=true, it has both 'rows' (from text_source_bundle) and 'other_bundle_rows' (from other_bundle) inside source_data -- translate BOTH independently, never assume they mean the same thing, never reuse one translation for the other. Where a table is false, translate 'rows' once.
rules: Preserve every number, percentage, and quantity in the source exactly -- never recalculate or round.

Preserve any <color=#RRGGBB>...</color> tags exactly (same hex, same open/close pairing) if present in a row -- this batch was checked and has no {0}/${0}$-style placeholders, but double-check each row yourself rather than assuming none exist.
Empty strings stay empty -- never invent content for a blank field.
Keep status-effect NAMES short (1-3 words, UI-label length: e.g. burn, poison, bleed, shock/stun, ignite). Descriptions can be short phrases/sentences matching typical mobile-game tooltip terseness.
Reuse the glossary below wherever the same Chinese term appears. Add any new terms you coin (especially buff/status-effect vocabulary) to a 'glossary_additions' object in your output.
If a term is genuinely ambiguous, pick your best interpretation and record it in an 'uncertain_notes' array in your output -- don't silently drop or paraphrase away something you don't understand.
Do not build, patch, install, or touch any game file, ADB, or emulator -- this file contains only text. Your job is purely to produce correct, complete translated JSON.
instructions.output_format: Produce translated text for every table under source_data.tables, preserving the exact same keys/shape (key columns copied verbatim, 'rows' translated, and 'other_bundle_rows' translated independently wherever the source has it). Include 'glossary_additions' and 'uncertain_notes' in your output.
instructions.delivery: This is going into the SAME ongoing cloud session/repo that already translated the Building/Ships/Missions batch -- just add your output there (e.g. translated/batch2_buffs_status_effects_translated.json), no new repo needed.

glossary.note: Terminology already established while translating the Home/housing tables (v262). Reuse these exact English terms whenever the same Chinese term appears in the ships/building/missions batch, for consistency across the whole game. Add new terms you establish for naval/ship/mission vocabulary to this file as you go.

likely_needed_for_this_batch_suggestions.note: These are suggestions based on sample rows already seen in the source JSON, not mandates -- use your judgment, but stay internally consistent once you pick a rendering.
likely_needed_for_this_batch_suggestions.洗练: Refine / Refinement (a stat-reroll mechanic, not the same as the housing Refinery building)

header.note_on_bundle_divergence: Like the Building/Ships/Missions batch before it, most tables here have tabledata.ab and tabledata_v1.ab copies that are NOT text-identical for shared keys. TableBuffGroupRule is the most extreme case in this batch: of ~1780 shared ids, ~150 hold COMPLETELY DIFFERENT buff/skill names between the two bundles (different attacks entirely, not just reworded text), and each bundle also has several hundred ids the other bundle lacks outright. TableSeaExploreBuffGroup and TablecampBuff are also highly divergent (one bundle has far fewer/placeholder rows than the other). See per-table 'content_diverges_between_bundles', 'other_bundle_rows' and the 'warnings' list below.
